about: Worked examples: a goal, the parameters that reach it, and why. Unlisted parameters use their defaults. Start from the closest recipe and adjust.

recipes.why: prism with 4 sides gives a square frame; membraneFaces 2 plates every face except the top. height 1.6 is the tallest a prism gets (≈ 0.8 × width).
bulge 1 turns the octagon into a circle; membraneFaces 2 leaves the top open.
Same as the vase with a low height.

recipes.goal: Solid lump with a bowl-shaped hollow
recipes.why: A single blob is solid; a hole with holeDepth < 1 leaves a bottom.
loop with bulge 1 is a circle; a thick radius makes it a torus.
depth squashes the circle front-to-back into an ellipse.
Negative bulge pulls the pentagon edges inward into a star; membrane fills it.
lattice subdivides each face; square profile gives crisp bars.
Spikes grow from skeleton points, so lattice is used to create many points; membranes close the body.
Positive taper thickens the ends of the line.
bipyramid with 4 sides is an octahedron; no membrane leaves the wire frame.

recipes.goal: Cage with solid top and bottom
recipes.why: membraneFaces 3 plates only the horizontal faces; lattice fills the open sides.
rnoise acts on lines (not blob balls), so a star of thick arms with lumps and bends reads as organic.

limits: No sphere skeleton: bulge only bends horizontal polygon edges, so a round cage comes out cylindrical.
No legs: a tripod or stand cannot be made directly.
No combining shapes: handles or attachments need two generated meshes joined elsewhere.
No inward-curved floors: a dish is flat-bottomed.
